must_remember: Scalar product $A \cdot B = AB \cos(\theta)$ results in a scalar quantity and is commutative.
Vector product $|A \times B| = AB \sin(\theta)$ results in a vector and is anticommutative: $A \times B = -(B \times A)$.
Condition for two non-zero vectors to be perpendicular is $A \cdot B = 0$.
Condition for two non-zero vectors to be parallel or antiparallel is $A \times B = 0$.
Scalar triple product $A \cdot (B \times C)$ represents the volume of the parallelepiped formed by the three vectors.
Vector triple product is evaluated using the BAC-CAB rule: $A \times (B \times C) = B(A \cdot C) - C(A \cdot B)$.

glossary.meaning: Also known as the dot product, defined as $A \cdot B = AB \cos(\theta)$.
Also known as the cross product, defined by $|A \times B| = AB \sin(\theta)$ with direction given by the right-hand rule.
Expressed as $A \cdot (B \times C)$, yielding a scalar equal to the volume of the parallelepiped.
Expressed as $A \times (B \times C)$, yielding a vector lying in the plane of the latter two vectors.
